newsitem.title: USA: ValuJet debt up on news can resume flights.
newsitem.headline: ValuJet debt up on news can resume flights.

text.p: ValuJet Inc debt gained more than three points after the U.S. Department of Transportation said the low-cost carrier's planes can return to the skies, dealers said on Thursday.
Roughly half an hour after the much-anticipated announcement, price talk on ValuJet's $150 million 10.25 percent notes due 2001 had gained to a 90 bid, 91 offer.
While quotes were actively bid higher, few dealers said they had seen the completion of actual trades at these new levels.
When asked if the notes' price could move higher by Thursday's close, one dealer said: "I don't think it has moved from there (90 bid, 91 offer) and that was 20 minutes ago."
The notes closed at a tight 86-1/2 bid, 86-7/8 offer market on Thursday, another dealer said.
The price of ValuJet debt slid 20 points to an 80 bid following news its Flight 592 crashed in the Florida Everglades on May 11.
Ensuing negative press and the June 17 grounding of the fleet after a DOT safety inspection of its operations caused the notes to bottom out at a mid-60's bid in June.
Standard & Poor's said in August ValuJet's B-minus corporate credit and CCC-plus senior unsecured ratings remain on watch with negative implication, where they were placed May 13, 1996.
Moody's cut the carrier's senior unsecured rating to B3 from B1 and placed the rating under review for a further possible downgrade in June.
